INITIAL SYMPTOMS:
User Sarah Chen states remote access VPN fails during morning sign-in.
The Cisco AnyConnect / Secure Client client initializes, prompts for Azure MFA push,
user approves MFA notification on mobile, but VPN immediately terminates with:
"Authentication failed: client certificate invalid or expired. Contact your system administrator."

WORK NOTES & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- 2026-11-03 08:30 EST - Tech Rachel: Connected to user machine via Remote Assistance.
- 2026-11-03 08:35 EST - Opened certmgr.msc (Current User Certificate Store).
  Navigated to Certificates - Current User > Personal > Certificates.
  Identified User Authentication Certificate issued by 'Enterprise-SubCA-01.synthetic-test.local'.
  Status: Expired on 2026-11-01 23:59:59 UTC.
- 2026-11-03 08:42 EST - Attempted manual certificate renewal via Certificate MMC snap-in.
  Received RPC error 0x800706BA because user was off-network and cannot reach on-prem Issuing CA RPC endpoints.
- 2026-11-03 08:50 EST - Implemented temporary bypass:
  Configured temporary fallback VPN tunnel group 'Emergency-CloudMFA-Profile' which validates Azure AD SAML assertion instead of machine certificate.
  User successfully authenticated to emergency VPN tunnel.
- 2026-11-03 09:05 EST - Once connected to emergency tunnel, ran certificate auto-enrollment command in elevated PowerShell:
  certutil -pulse
  Restart-Service CryptSvc
- 2026-11-03 09:12 EST - Verified new certificate issued with validity through 2027-11-03.
- 2026-11-03 09:18 EST - Disconnected emergency VPN. Tested primary corporate VPN profile 'Corp-Standard-VPN'.
  Authentication succeeded seamlessly using renewed client certificate.

ROOT CAUSE:
Client certificate reached its 1-year expiration date while user was working remotely for 3 weeks without connecting to enterprise network, preventing scheduled Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) auto-enrollment.

VERIFICATION:
Tested connection from primary profile. Ping to internal resource 192.0.2.10 successful. Status: Closed.
